The other top-level *.md and a few docs/*.md are WORKING / DESIGN notes written while building features. Many describe features that are now DONE (merged into code + USER_GUIDE + ROADMAP), so the note is redundant scratch. Some may still hold open items not captured anywhere.
docs/archive/ already holds superseded docs (commercial_v1_roadmap.md, driver_ROADMAP.md, TODO.md).

YOU ARE AUDITING ONE DOC (READ-ONLY - do not edit, move, or delete any file): `one_elf_three_engines.md`

Steps:
1. Read `one_elf_three_engines.md` fully. Note its topic and any status it self-declares (DONE/SUPERSEDED/REMOVED/etc).
2. VERIFY the real status against the codebase - do not trust the doc:
   - `git log --oneline -- <relevant paths>` and `git log --oneline --all -S '<keyword>'` for the feature it describes.
   - Search ROADMAP.md for the matching feature id / FR row and its Status (done/partial/not-started/REMOVED).
   - Search docs/USER_GUIDE.md for whether the feature is documented for users.
   - Search docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb for related L-ids.
   - Confirm the implementation + tests actually exist in the tree (grep code).
3. Decide verified_status: done (implemented, tested, in USER_GUIDE/ROADMAP) | partial | open | stale-superseded | canonical-keep | unknown.
4. List content_absorbed_in: where the doc's info now lives. If the feature is DONE and fully captured in code+USER_GUIDE+ROADMAP, the doc is redundant.
5. List open_items the doc still records, and for EACH say whether it is already_tracked_in ROADMAP (feature id) or limitations (L-id) or NOT-tracked, and the route (limitations-notebook / TODO / roadmap / already-tracked / none).
6. recommendation:
   - delete: feature DONE and fully absorbed; doc is pure redundant scratch with NO untracked open items.
   - extract-then-delete: doc has open items NOT tracked anywhere - they must be routed to limitations/TODO/roadmap first, then the doc can go.
   - archive: historical value (a removed-feature rationale, a superseded plan worth keeping for provenance) -> move to docs/archive/.
   - keep: still an active/canonical reference.
Be concrete in evidence (real commit hashes, file paths, section names). Return ONLY the structured object.

1	# one_elf_three_engines: compile once, run on fast / cycle / hybrid
2	
3	Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
4	tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.
5	
6	Design (the "vplat" device ABI): the binary talks only to devices that BOTH
7	engines model at the same addresses:
8	
9	| Channel | Address | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
10	|---|---|---|---|
11	| stdio   | UART2 16550, THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034 | serial_hd(0) | uart.hpp -> host stdout |
12	| exit    | SimControl @0xe0080000 (code u32) | NEW device (F2) | sim_control.hpp |
13	| file io | HTIF magicmem cmd @0xe0080010 | NEW (F4, stretch) | sim_control.hpp 17 syscalls |
14	
15	The guest runtime is one newlib stub layer (`vplat_syscalls.c`) replacing
16	`-lgloss_vh`; no semihosting, no engine detection (impossible anyway: hybrid
17	migrates the process mid-run).
18	
19	## Features
20	
21	| id | name | state | description | key files | deps |
22	|----|------|-------|-------------|-----------|------|
23	| F1 | vplat-runtime | done | newlib stubs over UART/SimControl/HTIF; `vplat_hello.elf` prints + exits 0 on `--model cycle` | tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c, tests/fixtures/Makefile, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh | - |
24	| F2 | qemu-sim-control | done | SimControl MMIO device in the QEMU fork at 0xe0080000 (exit codes, putchar, NEWLINE); same ELF prints + exits 0 on `--model fast` | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f2.sh | F1 |
25	| F3 | hybrid-same-elf | done | same ELF on `--model hybrid --trigger pc` (`--pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end`): "hello" prints from the vsim leg via the modeled UART, window_cycles + PASS | tests/vplat/test_vplat_f3.sh (no driver change expected) | F1, F2 |
26	| F4 | qemu-htif | done | HTIF file-syscall dispatch in the QEMU device (open/read/write/...; pico_stat layout) so fopen/fwrite parity holds; `vplat_file.elf` passes on fast + cycle | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f4.sh | F2 |
27	| F5 | docs | done | USER_GUIDE section + tutorial notebook: one build cell, three run cells | docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb | F1-F3 |
28	| F6 | e2e-default-engine | done | `run_e2e.sh` defaults VSIM_BIN to the canonical single-hart `sim_ax45mpv_premium` (hsim's pinned default) instead of alphabetically-first `sim_*`; suite 35/35 with no env override | scripts/run_e2e.sh, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f6.sh | - |
29	
30	## Notes
31	
32	- vsim needs zero changes: UART, SimControl exit, and HTIF already exist
33	  (verilator/src/platform/{uart,sim_control}.hpp).
34	- The driver needs zero changes: `fast` already propagates QEMU's exit code,
35	  `cycle` already returns `sim.run()` (sim_control exits), `hybrid` already
36	  handles csr markers.
37	- Exit-code map (mirrors vsim sim_control.hpp): 0x01234567 FINISHED/0x01234568
38	  PASSED/0x01234571 SKIPPED -> 0; 0x01234569 FAILED/0x01234570 WARNING -> 1;
39	  raw < 256 -> that code. crt0.S's secondary-hart SKIPPED write becomes legal
40	  on QEMU too.
41	- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM
42	  behind the cache); harmless on QEMU.
43	- FINDING (e2e, pre-existing; FIXED by F6): `run_e2e.sh` used to default
44	  VSIM_BIN to the alphabetically FIRST `verilator/build/sim_*`, which since
45	  the 06-09 engine rebuild is `sim_ax45mpv_mp2` -- a 2-core config. On it
46	  every crt0-based C fixture fails: hart 1 runs crt0 from reset on the vsim
47	  leg, takes the `mhartid != 0` path, writes SKIPPED (0x01234571) to
48	  SimControl and stops the sim before hart 0's drain (expected exit 200,
49	  got 0). Scope decision: the fixtures and harness stay SINGLE-HART; the fix
50	  is the default engine pick (F6), not multicore-proofing the fixtures.
51	  Multicore engines remain usable via an explicit `VSIM_BIN=...` for code
52	  written for them.
53	- FINDING (F2): the csr markers are NOT engine-portable. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB
54	  on the Andes core; the EXIT marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) sets ILM-enable with
55	  base 0, which shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run -> instruction fetches
56	  read zeroed ILM -> illegal-instruction trap loop (rt_c_hello.elf reproduces
57	  this on `--model fast` today). Hybrid runs are safe only because the exit
58	  marker retires on vsim, where the drain fires at retire. Portable binaries
59	  therefore delimit the ROI by PC symbols (say_hello / vplat_roi_end), and the
60	  hybrid leg uses `--trigger pc`.

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (marker HINT, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
21	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./andes-sim`

1230	## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)
1231	
1232	A binary linked with a semihosting libgloss (e.g. `-lgloss_vh`) can print
1233	only where a QEMU intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no
1234	semihosting, so a syscall inside the ROI traps there -- the old Phase-2
1235	"no syscalls inside the ROI" rule. The **vplat runtime** removes the
1236	per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
1237	(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
1238	engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
1239	and across a `hybrid` handoff, and a syscall inside the ROI works (it just
1240	adds its real cycles to the figure). Every in-tree C fixture links this
1241	runtime; nothing in the repo uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore.
1242	
1243	| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
1244	|---------|--------|------------------|------|
1245	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
1246	| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
1247	| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |
1248	
1249	The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandes_sim_runtime.a`. Build it once
1250	(`./andes-sim build --what runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
1251	then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
1252	no `-lgloss_vh`):
1253	
1254	```sh
1255	"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
1256	  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
1257	```
1258	
1259	`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
1260	`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
1261	`-specs=andes-sim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
1262	adds `-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
1263	list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
1264	libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.
1265	
1266	Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:
1267	
1268	```sh
1269	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andes-sim.ld \
1270	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
1271	  -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
1272	```
1273	
1274	Sources live in `runtime/` (crt0.S boot, trap.S + handler.c trap
1275	diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
1276	the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
1277	would never extract it from a `.a`.
1278	
1279	Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
1280	(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io); they are built
1281	with exactly the two-flag command above. Per-feature smoke tests live in
1282	`tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f9.sh`.
1283	
1284	Notes:
1285	
1286	- **Exit codes** stay below 256; the write to `0xe0080000` terminates the
1287	  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
1288	  (magic commands `0x01234567/68/71` map to 0, `0x01234569/70` to 1).
1289	- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine
1290	  process cwd; the QEMU device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.

## Repository Overview

Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).

Two Git submodules:
- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
- `tools/simpoint/` - SimPoint 3.2 (UCSD) clustering binary; pinned to upstream `17783e5`

Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).

## Build Commands

**Primary path (`./andes-sim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
first use), used in all user-facing docs. The retired Python driver is kept
as `hsim.py`, the byte-parity golden (`tests/andes_sim/parity.sh`); the
SimPoint pipeline (`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`,
`archive`, `replay`) still runs only there until the C++ port lands.

```sh
./andes-sim build                  # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
./andes-sim test                   # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
./andes-sim run --model fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc|icount] [--engine ID] <elf>
./andes-sim list <models|engines>
```

**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:

```sh
# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin -> simpoint)
source ./setup.sh

# Build individual components
./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT="$PWD/QEMU"  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree); QEMU_ROOT must be absolute (make -C chdirs first)
./scripts/build_simpoint.sh                          # SimPoint clustering binary (g++ on host)

# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture

# Clean
source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all]

Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.

| Channel | Address | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---|---|---|---|
| stdio   | UART2 16550, THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034 | serial_hd(0) | uart.hpp -> host stdout |
| exit    | SimControl @0xe0080000 (code u32) | NEW device (F2) | sim_control.hpp |
| file io | HTIF magicmem cmd @0xe0080010 | NEW (F4, stretch) | sim_control.hpp 17 syscalls |

The guest runtime is one newlib stub layer (`vplat_syscalls.c`) replacing
`-lgloss_vh`; no semihosting, no engine detection (impossible anyway: hybrid
migrates the process mid-run).

| id | name | state | description | key files | deps |
|----|------|-------|-------------|-----------|------|

| F5 | docs | done | USER_GUIDE section + tutorial notebook: one build cell, three run cells | docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb | F1-F3 |

- vsim needs zero changes: UART, SimControl exit, and HTIF already exist
  (verilator/src/platform/{uart,sim_control}.hpp).
- The driver needs zero changes: `fast` already propagates QEMU's exit code,
  `cycle` already returns `sim.run()` (sim_control exits), `hybrid` already
  handles csr markers.
- Exit-code map (mirrors vsim sim_control.hpp): 0x01234567 FINISHED/0x01234568

- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM

  `mhartid != 0` path, writes SKIPPED (0x01234571) to SimControl and stops

  `VSIM_BIN=$PWD/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium JOBS=8 bash
  scripts/run_e2e.sh` -> 35/35 pass.
- FINDING (F2): the csr markers are NOT engine-portable. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB
  on the Andes core; the EXIT marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) sets ILM-enable with
  base 0, which shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run -> instruction fetches
  read zeroed ILM -> illegal-instruction trap loop (rt_c_hello.elf reproduces
  this on `--model fast` today). Hybrid runs are safe only because the exit
  marker retires on vsim, where the drain fires at retire. Portable binaries
  therefore delimit the ROI by PC symbols (say_hello / vplat_roi_end), and the
  hybrid leg uses `--trigger pc`.

  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.

  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate

  landed.

  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`

  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16)."
